fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can confirm the correct property from the road.
• Mark the single driveway entry point clearly so arriving units can identify it quickly under low-visibility conditions.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles so responding units can reach the main residence and detached structure without stopping to reposition.
• Identify and mark a designated staging area within the parking area so multiple units can position without blocking the access drive.
• Trim vegetation along the access drive so it does not narrow the driveway width or obstruct the path to either structure.
• Cut back dense vegetation growing close to the main residence and detached structure so responders can move around the buildings without obstruction.
• Clear a walking path between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between buildings without pushing through overgrowth.
• Mark or post a simple site diagram at the driveway entrance showing the location of both structures, the water feature, and any rear access points.
• Post a visible warning at the driveway entrance identifying the water feature on the property so arriving responders are aware before moving across the lawn area at night or in low visibility.
• If a rear gate exists in the perimeter fencing, keep it unlocked and mark it so responders can locate an alternative exit route if the single access drive becomes blocked.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin trees within the cluster nearest to the structure to create more open space between the trees and the building.
• Remove shrubs that are growing directly against or touching the exterior walls of the structure.
• Trim the lower branches of scattered trees near the structure so branches do not hang close to the ground or roofline.
• Keep the area between individual tree clusters and the structure clear of low-growing shrubs and debris.
• Remove any dead or dry plant material from around the base of shrubs near the structure.
• Maintain the open terrain areas around the structure by preventing shrub or tree seedling growth from filling in those gaps.
• Thin shrubs growing along the edges of tree clusters closest to the structure to reduce the connection between the clusters and the building.
